title: Hip dislocated riding a freight train as a boy
summary: He crawled home half a mile after a freight-train accident; the leg healed shorter.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh boy. It gets down there. Well, you mentioned to me one day last week that you had some trouble with your hip when you were young. You talked about the injury in 1965 or '66, just before you moved in here. But did you also have an injury when you were young?

Well, my hip was knocked out of place. I guess I must have been around, oh... I left when I was around fourteen. It was down there... That must have been around 1913, '11, '12, somewhere around there. I was a young boy. I got my leg, my hip knocked out of place riding a freight train. I grabbed the freight train, on the freight train what do they call the last car....
Yes. And I grabbed that. I caught myself on a hobo from one town to another, and got my leg caught down in
the...they call it a trussle...a cattle(?) car...
The trestle. But I got my leg hooked down in there, and it was...

Dislocated... It broke. And I got up on that caboose... I made a mistake and stepped down in that catacomb(?) thing there, and I fell about...oh, I guess about four or five inches, or feet rather... And it was a good thing that another train wasn't behind me. I didn't fall between the tracks. I fell right on the side of them. If another train had been coming down there, it would have cut me in two. I just fell just like that.

That was round about, say, about a half-a-mile from where I lived. I had to crawl all the way back, because nobody knew where I was. I crawled from where the accident was; I crawled home a half-a-mile. It was dark, too; it must have been around six or seven o'clock at night. I could see snakes and things crawling in front of me. I had to cross a little sink-hole(?) pond and walk on a log to keep from, you know...
Then when I got there, my mother looked me, and she felt... I guess she felt sorry for me. She put me in a chair... She put me in a chair... During that time, you

didn't know about no doctors and all that stuff. She put me in a chair, and stood it ...(?)...(?)., put some bricks or rocks to put it up there and hold it. I stayed there I guess about a couple of months like that, and the thing just ...(?)..., you know. Right now, one of my legs is... This is the short one, this is the long one. One is about two inches shorter than the other. Instead of going like this, it tore (?) from there and stripped down in here, you know...
Yeah, it overlapped. And it grew like that. I came to New York in 19...I don't know what year it was...
